statement: For every input emails satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r and r equals, as an i64, the number of distinct byte strings in the set { norm(emails[i]) | 0 <= i < len(emails) }, where: at(e) is the unique index with e[at(e)] = '@'; local(e) = e[0..at(e)-1]; domain(e) = e[at(e)+1..len(e)-1]; prefix(e) is local(e) if local(e) contains no '+' byte, otherwise local(e)[0..p-1] where p is the first index with local(e)[p] = '+'; norm_local(e) is prefix(e) with every '.' byte deleted; and norm(e) is the byte string norm_local(e) followed by the byte '@' followed by domain(e). Thus r is exactly the number of different addresses that actually receive mail after applying the local-name dot and plus rules and leaving the domain unchanged.
preconditions: Let a valid input mean: len(emails) is between 1 and 100 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(emails), e = emails[i] has 1 <= len(e) <= 100; every byte of e is one of 'a'..'z', '+', '.', '@'; e contains exactly one byte '@'; the local part (bytes before '@') and domain part (bytes after '@') are both non-empty; local[0] != '+'; the domain ends with the four bytes '.', 'c', 'o', 'm'; and len(domain) >= 5 so at least one byte precedes the .com suffix. The input emails is a valid input.
